mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced business investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate indicates a weakening economy, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a strengthening economy and consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and corporate profits, which results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply chain and reduced economic output, leading to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases, it indicates a severe labor market contraction, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase and CPI (CPIAUCSL) remains stable, it signals strong consumer demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL changes < 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 1% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS does not increase
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) coupled with stable industrial production (INDPRO) signals a healthy economic expansion without overextension, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% in 6 months and INDPRO changes < 1%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and INDPRO on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
